t.1.31.1: There was a great ascetic of mighty austerities named Kuśa, born of Brahmā. In the princess of Vidarbha he begot four sons who were like himself.
t.1.31.2: Kuśa, wishing to have them carry out the duty of kṣatriyas, spoke to his sons Kuśāmba, Kuśanābha, Ādhūrtarajasa and Vasu, who were radiant, of great energy, most righteous and truthful in speech.
t.1.31.3: Having heard the words of Kuśa, all four of those best of men, esteemed by the world, then undertook the founding of cities.
t.1.31.4: The greatly splendid Kuśāmba founded the city of Kauśāmbī, while the righteous-souled Kuśanābha built the excellent city of Mahodaya.
t.1.31.5: O Rāma, the lord of the earth Ādhūrtarajasa built the excellent city Dharmāraṇya, and King Vasu built Girivraja.
t.1.31.6: This land, O Rāma, is Vasumatī, belonging to that great-souled Vasu; these five excellent mountains shine all around.
t.1.31.7: The lovely river, the renowned Sumāgadhī, flowed toward the Māgadhas; set amid the five foremost mountains, it shines like a garland.
t.1.31.9: And the royal sage Kuśanābha, righteous of soul, begot a hundred peerless daughters upon Ghṛtācī, O delight of the Raghus.
t.1.31.8: This indeed, O Rāma, is the Māgadhī of that great-souled Vasu, traversed of old, O Rāma, rich in excellent fields and garlanded with crops.
t.1.31.10: Those maidens, rich in youth, beautiful and finely adorned, came to the garden grounds, like flashes of lightning in the rainy season.
t.1.31.11: Singing, dancing and playing on musical instruments, O Rāghava, adorned with the finest ornaments, they attained the highest delight.
t.1.31.12: Then those maidens, lovely in every limb and unmatched on earth in beauty, came to the pleasure garden, like stars amid the clouds.
t.1.31.13: Seeing those maidens, endowed with every virtue and possessed of beauty and youth, the all-pervading Vāyu spoke these words.
t.1.31.14: I desire all of you; you shall become my wives. Let your human nature be cast off, and you shall obtain a long life.
t.1.31.15: Having heard those words of Vāyu, whose deeds are never wearied, the hundred maidens laughed his speech to scorn and then said:
t.1.31.16: O best of the gods, you move within all beings; and we all know your power. Why, then, do you treat us with contempt?
t.1.31.17: We, the daughters of Kuśanābha, are all capable, O best of the gods, of toppling you, a god, from your station, but we guard our ascetic merit.
t.1.31.18: May that foolish time never come! Do not disregard our truthful father; in accordance with dharma we wait upon a svayaṃvara.
t.1.31.20: Hearing those words of theirs, Vāyu, the mighty and blessed lord, became exceedingly wrathful; entering into all their limbs, he broke them.
t.1.31.19: For our father is our lord; he is indeed our supreme deity. He to whom our father gives us will be our husband.
t.1.31.21: Those maidens, deformed by Vāyu, entered the palace of the king. Seeing them deformed, the king, deeply agitated, then spoke these words.
t.1.31.22: What is this? Let it be told, daughters: who disregards dharma? By whom have you all been made hunchbacked, that you writhe and do not speak?
